reasons: Cited Section 13 (p0078) provides automatic renewal for successive one-year terms — not multi-year — with either party, including Client, able to block renewal on written notice given 30 days before the end of the then-current year. That satisfies the preferred position's material terms (12-month renewal, ≤30-day customer opt-out) and is well inside the 60-day fallback ceiling and far from the 90-day/multi-year walk-away.

The claimed status is 'compliant' and, consistent with that, no redline was applied (redline text is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment was generated — appropriate treatment for a clause retained as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue.

The failed deterministic check ('non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days — number not found') is a phrasing artifact: the clause spells the window as 'thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year', which the regex did not capture. Substance clearly meets the threshold.

The two shortfalls the rationale flags — no Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal and no CPI/3% (or ≤5%) cap on post-year-one uplifts (Section 6 only freezes Hosting Services costs for one year plus a most-favoured-rate commitment) — are exactly the kind of minor sub-elements (missing reminder mechanic, missing price-uplift cap) the playbook directs be noted in the rationale rather than raised as independent deviations. Correctly handled and accurately described.
